ghosts.name: Sakura and Unyuu
aliases: さくらとも呼ばれるひと
ghosts.author: 黒衣鯖人
ghosts.download_status: original distribution ended; no preservation download listed
ghosts.technical_context: The 2000-05-25 prototype preceded Unyuu, who was added on 2000-09-15. The character and software names changed repeatedly. This original Nise-Haruna/Nin'i-tan incarnation is distinct from the later Mikage Sakura redesign.
ghosts.description: The original default character at the beginning of the lineage that became Ukagaka. Sakura-then known as Nise-Haruna and later Nin'i-tan-was created by 黒衣鯖人; Saxyun supplied the character artwork. Unyuu joined her in September 2000.

ghosts.name: Futaba and Tadakichi-san
ghosts.author: 閑馬永空
ghosts.download_status: original and 2018 redistribution downloads are currently unavailable
ghosts.technical_context: Futaba became the bundled default character with 何か period “redo” zero on 2001-08-05. The contemporary redo terminology reference describes two selectable dialogue implementations: the Fake by 閑馬永空 and the Slayer by 橋本孔明. Period 284 replaced Futaba as the default on 2001-11-22. Surviving later files contain shells only, not the complete ghost.
ghosts.description: The second default character pair in the early Ukagaka lineage. Futaba and her creature companion Tadakichi-san were bundled with 何か during the period between the original Sakura incarnation and the later default Sakura redesign.

image.alt: Futaba standing beside the yellow creature Tadakichi-san

sources.notes: Contemporary reference identifies the characters as 双葉 and ただきち and credits the Fake to 閑馬永空 and the Slayer to 橋本孔明.

sources.title: 「伺か」システム用語集 “MATERIA” 版
sources.notes: Describes Futaba as the bundled character that replaced the earlier Sakura when 何か was formally released.

ghosts.name: Naru and Yuuka
ghosts.author: 楠見くれあ
ghosts.technical_context: Naru began as a PersonaWare persona and was test-released as the ghost 偽奈留 on 2001-01-21. The archived creator site lists Naru m0.15a on 2001-12-06. Contemporary reporting records a development-continuation announcement in July 2002 and a new site that August. No later package is currently listed.
ghosts.description: An early bilingual ghost featuring the gentle Naru and her tiny companion Yuuka. Naru was one of the period's so-called Four Angels and grew from an earlier PersonaWare persona into a recognizable early Ukagaka character.

image.alt: Naru in a grey school uniform standing beside the tiny white Yuuka
image.credit: Naru and Yuuka preview published with a contemporary June 2002 review; credited there to creator and artist 楠見くれあ

sources.title: etwas - archived Naru distribution page

sources.notes: Contemporary review identifies Naru and Yuuka, German dialogue, Four Angels status, PersonaWare origin, and 楠見くれあ as both developer and artist; later annotations record renewed development activity in 2002.

ghosts.author: ls (Araya Kawakami)

She is a separate record from the discontinued 2000–2001 Nise-Haruna/Nin'i-tan incarnation. The surviving official download is the complete MATERIA period 583 Windows package, not a standalone ghost archive.
ghosts.description: The blue-haired Sakura redesign introduced as MATERIA-B's default shell in March 2002, accompanied by Unyuu. The original site still distributes the period 583 MATERIA package containing this default ghost.

ghosts.name: Seriko
ghosts.author: MIY
ghosts.companion: Maruchii (まるちい; also written まるちぃ)
ghosts.download_status: full 2004 ghost package preserved by the Wayback Machine; no current official distribution listed
ghosts.technical_context: Seriko first appeared as a skin for Nise-Haruna on 2000-12-20 and later developed into a complete ghost. Her animated second shell was described in contemporary coverage as the first animated ghost shell in the scene. The name SERIKO was subsequently adopted for Ukagaka's general shell-animation specification. The preserved 2004 package identifies both the ghost and shell creator as MIY.
ghosts.description: A foundational early character featuring the low-energy Seriko and her tiny companion Maruchii. Beginning as a Nise-Haruna skin before becoming a full ghost, Seriko became especially influential through her animated artwork: the Ukagaka shell-animation specification took its name from her.

image.alt: Seriko in a red coat standing beside the tiny Maruchii seated on a wheeled platform
image.credit: Seriko and Maruchii preview published with a contemporary June 2002 review; credited there to creator and artist MIY

download.heading: Historical archived package
download.notes: Preserved from the creator's original domain. The ZIP contains the complete ghost, shell, scripts, and the legacy executable library misaka.dll. Treat it as historical software rather than modern supported software.

sources.title: The History of Ukagaka - Nise-Haruna chronology
sources.notes: Mirror of a 2002 chronology dating EXTRA STAGE's first Seriko skin to 2000-12-20 and documenting the January 2001 animation implementation associated with her.

sources.title: 2002/06/24 - 伺かゴーストれびゅー そにょ1！
sources.notes: Contemporary review identifies MIY as developer and artist, describes Seriko and Maruchii's To Heart-derived premise, calls the second shell the scene's first animated ghost, and records Seriko 4 beta 3 as stalled in June 2002.

ghosts.name: Taromati - Kikka and Towa
ghosts.download_status: Taromati2 is available from its long-running proxy distribution page
ghosts.shiori: MISAKA in the original; AYA in Taromati2
ghosts.technical_context: Taromati is the formal ghost title; Kikka and Towa are its characters. The original Taromati was formally released on 2003-11-10. Taromati2, released on 2007-07-21, is a substantial rewrite rather than merely a replacement shell, but retains the same character pair. The distribution page explicitly states that its administrator is not the ghost creator and credits production to 8.
ghosts.description: A long-lived classic ghost pairing the silver-haired Kikka with Towa, a black cat who can also appear in human form. Taromati began in 2003 and received a major second-generation rewrite in 2007, accompanied by revised default artwork and an extensive collection of additional shells.

ghosts.author: とわ
ghosts.artist: D4 北野チェき (original ASCII art); みやま / MIY (bundled color shell)
ghosts.download_status: complete original ghost package preserved by the Wayback Machine; original host closed in March 2026
ghosts.technical_context: The original 54 uses an ASCII-art default shell derived from work by D4 北野チェき, with permission recorded in the package readme. The archive also bundles the widely recognizable MIY Color shell by みやま / MIY. Package metadata names the secondary character slot 540, though surviving documentation does not describe 540 as a conventional visible companion.
ghosts.description: An unusual classic centered on a quiet girl whose original appearance is drawn as large-scale ASCII art. The later bundled MIY Color shell gave 54 a more conventional illustrated form, and a remarkable number of artists subsequently created alternate shells for her.

image.alt: Windows desktop screenshot showing 54 in the MIY Color shell beside her original ASCII-art appearance
image.credit: Screenshot from the archived original distribution page, showing the bundled MIY Color shell at left and original ASCII-art shell at right

download.heading: Historical archived package
download.notes: Complete package from the archived original distribution page. It contains legacy executable components, scripts, artwork, and a balloon. Treat it as historical software rather than modern supported software.

english.summary: Project54_Eng is a usable partial English edition of AG36's 54-derived ghost. It is relevant to visitors looking for an English 54 experience, but it does not translate Towa's original ghost.

related_projects.title: AG36's Project54 / 54みたいの

ghosts.name: THE TOXIC WALTZ
ghosts.author: wat / わた臓
ghosts.download_status: restored editions preserved by the Internet Archive; original development and support ended
ghosts.technical_context: The package identifies the ghost as THE TOXIC WALTZ and its characters as 毒子 and ほねゅう. 毒子 is conventionally read Busuko; Doku-ko also appears as an English-language spelling. The surviving readmes describe a restored edition based largely on the March 2004 contents, covering work made in 2001–2004 and revived in 2006. A 2010 package replaces one bundled network library but otherwise retains the 2006 restored edition.
ghosts.description: A metal-themed supernatural-family ghost starring Busuko and her skeletal companion Honeyuu. THE TOXIC WALTZ became known for energetic dialogue and an unusually large, elaborate set of sometimes grotesque character animations that could be demanding on contemporary computers.

image.alt: Busuko wearing a black and red outfit in the default THE TOXIC WALTZ artwork

download.heading: Historical preserved package
download.notes: Third-party preservation copy of the 2010 restored edition. The package includes legacy executable components; treat it as historical software rather than modern supported software. Earlier 2006 restored packages are also retained on the item page.
